# Module `lune_ui_core::text_edit`

[API reference](../INDEX.md) / parent [`lune_ui_core`](index.md)

The text editing engine: caret, selection, navigation, undo and redo, clipboard commands and
the preedit an input method composes. It is pure: the app owns the text and passes it to
every call, the layout answers the geometry through [`EditLayout`](text_edit.md#trait.EditLayout), and time arrives as an
argument. A widget maps [`FocusEvent`](input.md#enum.FocusEvent)s with [`EditCommand::from_event`](text_edit.md#method.EditCommand.from_event) and calls
[`TextEdit::apply`](text_edit.md#method.TextEdit.apply).

The text is read through [`EditText`](text_edit.md#trait.EditText) and changed through [`EditBuffer`](text_edit.md#trait.EditBuffer): a `String` as it
always was, a [`CodeDoc`](code_doc.md#struct.CodeDoc) at a cost that does not follow the
document's size. Every rule here serves both (D180).

Every offset in this module is a char offset; the `TextSystem` queries use bytes of the spec's
text, and [`SpecLayout`](text_edit.md#struct.SpecLayout) turns one into the other at that seam, with the two private helpers
`byte_of` and `char_of` that also index the string when an edit changes it.

Offsets are total: any caret, anchor or query offset past the end or inside a grapheme is
clamped, never a panic.

Source: `crates/lune-ui-core/src/text_edit.rs:1`

The edit state of one text: caret and anchor as char offsets, the undo and redo logs, the
preferred x of vertical motion, the preedit, and the fingerprint of the last text it saw. The

<a id="trait.EditLayout"></a>
### Trait `EditLayout`

```rust
pub trait EditLayout { .. }
```

What the engine asks of the text's layout. Offsets are chars. `caret`, `hit` and `lines` read
the laid-out text, which the caller keeps equal to the text it passes to the engine;
`boundaries` reads the `text` it is given, so it also serves text not yet in the layout.

Source: `crates/lune-ui-core/src/text_edit.rs:76`

**Required items**

- <a id="tymethod.EditLayout.boundaries"></a>`fn boundaries(&mut self, text: &str, unit: Unit) -> Vec<usize>`

  The sorted boundaries of `unit` in `text`, including 0 and the char count.

- <a id="tymethod.EditLayout.caret"></a>`fn caret(&mut self, offset: usize) -> CaretPos`

  Where the caret sits at `offset`.

- <a id="tymethod.EditLayout.hit"></a>`fn hit(&mut self, pos: (f32, f32)) -> usize`

  The offset nearest to `pos`, in logical px from the text's top-left corner.

- <a id="tymethod.EditLayout.lines"></a>`fn lines(&mut self) -> Vec<LineSpan>`

  The visual lines, top to bottom, with `start` and `end` in chars.

**Provided items**

- <a id="method.EditLayout.extend_hit"></a>`fn extend_hit(&mut self, pos: (f32, f32), at: usize, bounds: &[usize]) -> usize`

  Where a drag that extends a selection ends at `pos`. `at` is what [`Self::hit`](text_edit.md#tymethod.EditLayout.hit) answered,
  snapped to a grapheme boundary, and `bounds` the sorted grapheme boundaries around it.

  A wrapped row runs straight into the next, so its end offset shows on the next row and
  `hit` stops at the row's last grapheme: a drag right of the row would leave that grapheme
  out. When `at` is that last grapheme's start and the point is past its middle, the answer
  is the next boundary, which is on the next row. The grapheme's width is taken from the one
  before it on the row (a row of one grapheme counts the point right of its start). Anything
  else is `at`: a hard-broken row keeps its line break out of a drag. A plain click does not
  call this, so its caret stays on the row it was pressed on.

- <a id="method.EditLayout.lines_near"></a>`fn lines_near(&mut self, _at: usize, _reach: isize) -> Vec<LineSpan>`

  The visual lines around `at`, top to bottom, as [`Self::lines`](text_edit.md#tymethod.EditLayout.lines) gives them: at least the
  line that shows `at`, the lines from it to `reach` lines away (negative is up), and one
  more on each side where there is one. A layout of a long document answers only these.

- <a id="method.EditLayout.page_rows"></a>`fn page_rows(&self) -> usize`

  How many lines a page motion crosses.

<a id="trait.EditText"></a>
### Trait `EditText`

```rust
pub trait EditText { .. }
```

What the engine reads of a text. Offsets are chars, and all of them are total: past the end
clamps. A reader of a long document answers each call without walking the document.

Source: `crates/lune-ui-core/src/text_edit.rs:145`

**Required items**

- <a id="tymethod.EditText.char_len"></a>`fn char_len(&self) -> usize`

  How many chars the text holds.

- <a id="tymethod.EditText.fingerprint"></a>`fn fingerprint(&self) -> u64`

  A value that changes whenever the text does, which is how the engine sees an external
  change.

- <a id="tymethod.EditText.slice"></a>`fn slice(&self, chars: Range<usize>) -> String`

  The text of chars `chars`.

- <a id="tymethod.EditText.window"></a>`fn window(&self, at: usize) -> (usize, &str)`

  A slice around char `at` and the char offset it starts at; it holds `at`, and it starts
  and ends where text segmentation does not reach across (the whole text, or whole lines).
  Grapheme motions and snapping read this window of the caret. A word motion reads it too,
  and the windows past it until it finds a word, so a text that answers less than the whole
  of itself costs a motion one window per stretch it crosses: see
  [`CodeDoc`](code_doc.md#struct.CodeDoc).

<a id="constant.MAX_SHAPED_INSERT"></a>
### Constant `MAX_SHAPED_INSERT`

```rust
pub const MAX_SHAPED_INSERT: usize = 1_048_576;
```

The most bytes a widget that shapes its whole text takes in one insert (a paste, an assistive
`SetValue`, an input method's commit); a longer one is refused whole, never cut. The text field
and the text area build one spec of all their text, so what they take costs in proportion: a
field about 25 ms a frame and 290 MB at 1 MiB, an area about 0.4 s to first draw and 430 MB (and
at the clipboard adapter's 32 MiB cap 10 to 16 s and 10 to 14 GB, extrapolated; measured and
recorded in D232 and D233). They set it through [`EditFlags::max_insert`](text_edit.md#structfield.EditFlags.max_insert); the code editor draws
only the lines in view and leaves it off, so it takes what the adapter lets through. An app's own
`max_chars` still applies below it.

Source: `crates/lune-ui-core/src/text_edit.rs:41`
